issues.description: The solution implementation of Developer.attend(...) has a different parameter list than both the problem specification and the template. The problem statement and template declare attend(course:) taking a single optional Course? parameter, but the solution defines attend(course: Course?, forCredit: Bool). Moreover, the solution's Client calls attend(course:) with only one argument, which is inconsistent with the solution's own method signature. This mismatch will confuse students and causes the solution code to be internally inconsistent and non-compilable as-is.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attend(...) method signature consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) change the solution's method to match the problem/template: `func attend(course: Course?)` (remove the extra `forCredit` parameter), or (B) if the extra parameter is intended, update the template, problem statement, and all call sites (e.g. Client) to include the new parameter (or give it a default value) so all artifacts agree. Recommended fix: remove `forCredit: Bool` from the solution's attend signature so it matches the template and problem description.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template define a Developer instance method attend(course:) that takes a single optional Course parameter. In the solution repository the method signature was changed to attend(course: Course?, forCredit: Bool), introducing an extra parameter (forCredit) and altering the expected call signature. This divergence breaks the one-to-one mapping between the requirement (and template stub) and the solution implementation, and may confuse students about the correct method to implement or call.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem and template by restoring the single-parameter signature: func attend(course: Course?) { ... }. Alternatively, if the additional forCredit parameter is intentional, give it a default value (forCredit: Bool = false) and update all calls (including Client.main()) and the problem statement to document the extra parameter so students are not confused.
